title: Numbers Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 25.

questions.question: Where did Israel abide when the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:1 states that Israel abode in Shittim when the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.

questions.question: What did the people do at the sacrifices of their gods according to Numbers 25?
options: They ate and bowed down to their gods
questions.correctAnswer: They ate and bowed down to their gods
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:2 says the people did eat and bowed down to their gods at the sacrifices.

questions.question: To which deity did Israel join themselves, causing the anger of the LORD to be kindled?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:3 records that Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor, which caused the LORD's anger to be kindled against Israel.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Moses to do with the heads of the people?
options: Take all the heads and hang them before the LORD against the sun
Burn all the heads outside the camp
Bury the heads in the valley
Throw the heads into the river
questions.correctAnswer: Take all the heads and hang them before the LORD against the sun
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:4 states the LORD told Moses to take all the heads of the people and hang them before the LORD against the sun to turn away His fierce anger.

questions.question: Who did Moses command to slay every man that was joined to Baalpeor?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:5 says Moses commanded the judges of Israel to slay every man that was joined to Baalpeor.

questions.question: What was happening before the door of the tabernacle when one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:6 mentions that the congregation of the children of Israel were weeping before the door of the tabernacle when the event happened.

questions.question: Who took a javelin and killed the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:7-8 states that Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, took a javelin and killed both the man and the woman.

questions.question: What was the result after Phinehas killed the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman?
options: The plague was stayed from the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The plague was stayed from the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:8 explains that after Phinehas's action, the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.

questions.question: How many died in the plague that came upon Israel?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:9 records that twenty and four thousand died in the plague.

questions.question: Who was the Israelite slain with the Midianitish woman?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:14 identifies the slain Israelite as Zimri, son of Salu.

questions.question: Who was the Midianitish woman slain with Zimri?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:15 gives the name of the Midianitish woman as Cozbi, daughter of Zur.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's anger was kindled against Israel because they joined themselves to Baalpeor.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:3 states the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel because they joined themselves to Baalpeor.

questions.question: True or False: Moses instructed the judges of Israel to spare those joined to Baalpeor.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:5 shows Moses told the judges to slay every man joined to Baalpeor, not to spare them.

questions.question: True or False: Phinehas's zeal for God turned away the LORD's wrath from the children of Israel.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:11 explains that Phinehas turned away the LORD's wrath by being zealous for God.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD commanded Moses to spare the Midianites despite their wiles.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:17 commands to vex and smite the Midianites for their deception; sparing them was not commanded.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What action did Phinehas take when he saw the Israelite man bringing a Midianitish woman before the congregation?
options: He took a javelin and killed both
questions.correctAnswer: He took a javelin and killed both
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:7-8 states that Phinehas took a javelin and thrust both the man and the woman through, which stopped the plague among Israel.

questions.question: How many Israelites died in the plague caused by their sin with the Moabite women?
questions.explanation: According to Numbers 25:9, twenty and four thousand died in the plague as a consequence of Israel's sin.

questions.question: What did the LORD say to Moses about Phinehas after he acted zealously?
options: He turned God's wrath away from Israel
He was to lead the army
questions.correctAnswer: He turned God's wrath away from Israel
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:11 explains that Phinehas, by his zeal for God, turned away the LORD's wrath from the children of Israel.

questions.question: What covenant did God give to Phinehas because of his zeal?
options: The covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood
The covenant of a great nation
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:12-13 states that God gave Phinehas a covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood because he was zealous for God and made atonement for Israel.

questions.question: Who was the Israelite man slain by Phinehas with the Midianitish woman?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:14 identifies the slain Israelite as Zimri, son of Salu, a prince among the Simeonites.

questions.question: What was the name of the Midianitish woman killed alongside Zimri?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:15 reveals the Midianitish woman as Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a chief in Midian.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give to Moses regarding the Midianites after the incident at Peor?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:17 commands Moses to vex and smite the Midianites because of their deceit that led Israel into sin.

questions.question: According to Numbers 25, why were the Midianites considered a threat to Israel?
options: They used wiles to beguile Israel into sin
questions.correctAnswer: They used wiles to beguile Israel into sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:18 explains that the Midianites vexed Israel with their wiles, causing them to sin through the matter of Peor and Cozbi.

questions.question: What does Numbers 25:9 teach about the consequences of sin in a community?
options: Sin can bring widespread death and judgment
Sin is easily forgiven without penalty
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can bring widespread death and judgment
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:9 reports a plague causing the death of 24,000, showing sin’s serious consequences for the entire community.

questions.question: How does Phinehas' action in Numbers 25:7-8 demonstrate the biblical virtue of zeal for God?
options: By ignoring sin to maintain peace
By taking decisive action to uphold God's holiness
By hiding the sin from the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: By taking decisive action to uphold God's holiness
questions.explanation: Phinehas acted zealously by decisively stopping sin to protect Israel’s covenant relationship with God (Numbers 25:7-8, 11-13).

questions.question: What promise does Numbers 25:12 give if one is zealous for God like Phinehas?
options: A covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood
questions.explanation: Verse 12 promises a covenant of peace to Phinehas for his zeal, further explained as an everlasting priesthood in verse 13.

questions.question: What does Numbers 25:5 reveal about Moses’ leadership response to the sin of Baalpeor?
options: He instructed judges to kill those joined to Baalpeor
questions.correctAnswer: He instructed judges to kill those joined to Baalpeor
questions.explanation: Moses commanded the judges to slay everyone joined to Baalpeor to turn away God's anger (Numbers 25:5).

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 25:3, Israel joined themselves to the worship of Baalpeor, which angered the LORD.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:3 clearly states that Israel joined themselves unto Baalpeor, provoking the LORD's anger against them.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 25:4 instructs Moses to pray for the people instead of taking any drastic action.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:4 commands Moses to take the heads of the people and hang them before the LORD to turn away His fierce anger, not merely to pray.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 25:8 shows that Phinehas’ act of killing the man and woman stopped the plague on Israel.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:8 states that after Phinehas killed the man and woman, the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 25.

questions.question: What covenant was given to Phinehas because of his zeal for God according to Numbers 25?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:13 states that Phinehas was given 'the covenant of an everlasting priesthood' because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for Israel.

questions.question: Who was the Israelite man that was slain with the Midianitish woman?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:14 identifies the slain Israelite as Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.

questions.question: What was the name and status of the Midianitish woman slain with Zimri?
options: Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a chief house head in Midian
Miriam, a daughter of a Levite
Rahab, a leader of Midianite women
questions.correctAnswer: Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a chief house head in Midian
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:15 states the Midianitish woman was Cozbi, daughter of Zur, who was head over a people and a chief house in Midian.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Moses concerning the Midianites after the plague?
options: Vex the Midianites, and smite them
Make peace treaties with the Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: Vex the Midianites, and smite them
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:17 records God's command to Moses to vex and smite the Midianites because they led Israel astray.

questions.question: What was the reason given for smiting the Midianites?
options: They beguiled Israel with their wiles in the matter of Peor and Cozbi
They refused to trade with Israel
They allied with the Moabites to wage war
questions.correctAnswer: They beguiled Israel with their wiles in the matter of Peor and Cozbi
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:18 explains the Midianites vexed Israel with their deceit, leading to the sin of Peor and involving Cozbi.

questions.question: What act of zeal did Phinehas perform that caused the plague to stop?
options: He killed the Israelite man and the Midianitish woman involved in sin
He prayed for mercy on the people
He led a sacrifice to God
questions.correctAnswer: He killed the Israelite man and the Midianitish woman involved in sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:7-8 recount how Phinehas took a javelin and killed both the Israelite man and the Midianitish woman, stopping the plague.

questions.question: How many people died in the plague caused by Israel's sin with Moabite women?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:9 states that 24,000 died in the plague due to Israel's sin.

questions.question: Which tribe did the slain Israelite, Zimri, belong to?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:14 identifies Zimri as a prince from a chief house among the Simeonites.

questions.question: What was happening in Israel that led to the anger of the LORD in Numbers 25?
options: The people committed whoredom with Moabite women and worshipped their gods
They refused to enter the promised land
They did not observe the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: The people committed whoredom with Moabite women and worshipped their gods
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:1-3 describes Israel's sin of whoredom with Moabite women and worship of their gods, provoking God's anger.

questions.question: True or False: The covenant given to Phinehas was conditional upon his descendants continuing to be zealous for God.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:13 emphasizes an 'everlasting priesthood' given to Phinehas and his seed because of his zeal; it does not state the covenant is conditional on descendants' behavior.

questions.question: True or False: The Midianite woman Cozbi was related to a prince of Midian.
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:15 and 25:18 identify Cozbi as the daughter of Zur, who was a head over a people and a chief house in Midian, indicating her princely relation.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of zeal for God seen in Phinehas' act?
questions.explanation: Psalm 69:9 states 'the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up,' echoing Phinehas' zeal in Numbers 25:11.

questions.question: What literary device is seen in the parallel structure involving Phinehas' act and God's covenant in Numbers 25?
options: Inclusio framing Phinehas' zeal with covenant promises
Chiasmus between the plague and the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing Phinehas' zeal with covenant promises
questions.explanation: The narrative in Numbers 25:7-13 creates an inclusio framing Phinehas' zealous act with God's covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'zealous' in Numbers 25:11 most closely means what?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'zealous' (קַנָּא, qanna) in Numbers 25:11 conveys intense fervor or ardent devotion for God.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references the zeal of Phinehas as an example of righteous jealousy for God?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:2 speaks of the zeal of the Israelites not being according to knowledge, indirectly referencing zeal like that shown by Phinehas in Numbers 25:11.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the initial sin committed by the Israelites while they were in Shittim according to Numbers 25:1?
options: They committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab
They refused to enter the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: They committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:1 explicitly states that Israel abode in Shittim and began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, illustrating the initial act of covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD’s anger at Israel’s joining with Baalpeor in Numbers 25:3?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:3 shows that the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel because they joined themselves to Baalpeor, revealing God's attribute of wrath against sin.

questions.question: What covenantal promise was given to Phinehas as a reward for his zeal in Numbers 25:12-13?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:12-13 describes how God gave Phinehas a covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood because of his zeal and atonement for Israel.

questions.question: How does Numbers 25:4-5 reveal the principle of communal responsibility and justice in Israel’s covenantal system?
options: It requires leaders to be judged separately
It commands the execution of those joined to Baalpeor by the judges
questions.correctAnswer: It commands the execution of those joined to Baalpeor by the judges
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:4-5 instructs Moses to have the heads of the offenders hung and commands the judges to slay those joined to Baalpeor, showing corporate justice and responsibility.

questions.question: Who was the Israelite leader that zealously intervened to stop the plague by killing the man and the Midianitish woman in Numbers 25:7-8?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:7-8 narrates how Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, took a javelin and killed the Israelite man and Midianitish woman, stopping the plague.

questions.question: According to Numbers 25:9, what was the consequence of Israel’s sin with the Moabites and Midianites?
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:9 states that twenty-four thousand died in the plague as a judgment for Israel’s sin with the foreign women.

questions.question: What does the combined teaching of Numbers 25:11 and Numbers 25:13 reveal about God’s response to zeal for His holiness?
options: God ignores zealotry in His people
God rewards zeal that turns away His wrath with covenant peace and priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards zeal that turns away His wrath with covenant peace and priesthood
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:11-13 shows that Phinehas' zeal turned away God's wrath, prompting a covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood as a reward, highlighting God's approval of zeal for His holiness.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught by the LORD’s command to ‘vex the Midianites’ in Numbers 25:17-18?
options: The doctrine of divine judgment against idolatry and seduction
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine judgment against idolatry and seduction
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:17-18 commands Israel to smite the Midianites because they seduced Israel into idolatry, teaching divine judgment upon those who lead God's people into sin.

questions.question: How does the act of Phinehas killing the Israelite and the Midianitish woman typologically foreshadow Christ’s work according to Numbers 25:7-8 and 11?
options: It foreshadows Christ as a conquering king
It foreshadows Christ’s zeal for God’s holiness and atonement
It foreshadows Christ’s priestly intercession without violence
It foreshadows Christ’s role as a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ’s zeal for God’s holiness and atonement
questions.explanation: Phinehas’ zeal and atoning act (Numbers 25:7-8, 11) prefigure Christ’s zeal for God’s holiness and His atoning sacrifice that turns away divine wrath (Hebrews 10:10-14).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's wrath in Numbers 25 is unjust and harsh. What does Numbers 25:3-5 and 11 actually teach about God's wrath?
options: God’s wrath is arbitrary and unprovoked
God’s wrath is a just response to covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry
God’s wrath is a myth and does not exist
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath is a just response to covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:3-5 and 11 show God's wrath is kindled because Israel joined Baalpeor, and it is turned away only by Phinehas’ zeal, teaching that God's wrath is just and aimed at covenant violation (Romans 1:18).

questions.question: What does the identification of Zimri and Cozbi in Numbers 25:14-15 signify about the nature of Israel’s sin?
options: It was a random act of rebellion by commoners
It was a politically and socially significant act involving leaders
It was a misunderstood cultural practice
It was an isolated incident with no larger impact
questions.correctAnswer: It was a politically and socially significant act involving leaders
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:14-15 names Zimri and Cozbi as leaders from chief houses, showing the sin involved prominent persons and therefore had grave covenant implications.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Numbers 25:1-3 have with Israel’s ongoing struggle in the wilderness?
options: It highlights Israel’s repeated covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry
It marks Israel’s final victory over enemies
It shows God’s abandonment of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights Israel’s repeated covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:1-3 fits the broader wilderness narrative where Israel repeatedly falls into idolatry, showing their persistent covenant failure and need for divine intervention (Exodus 32; Judges 2:11-15).

questions.question: What does the instruction in Numbers 25:4 to hang the heads of the offenders before the LORD illustrate about God’s holiness?
options: God tolerates sin among His people
God demands public accountability for sin
God hides sin from His people
questions.correctAnswer: God demands public accountability for sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:4 commands the heads of the offenders to be displayed before the LORD, emphasizing God’s demand for holiness and public accountability in His covenant community.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight emerges from combining Numbers 25:6 and Numbers 25:9 about sin and its consequences?
options: Corporate sin leads to corporate judgment
Sin can be ignored by God
questions.correctAnswer: Corporate sin leads to corporate judgment
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:6 shows a public act of sin, while 25:9 shows the resulting plague killing 24,000, teaching that Israel’s corporate sin brought collective judgment.

questions.question: According to Numbers 25:17-18, what is the theological reason for God's command to smite the Midianites?
options: Because they vexed Israel with their wiles and seduced them into sin
Because they were a military threat
Because they refused to marry Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Because they vexed Israel with their wiles and seduced them into sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 25:17-18 explains that the Midianites were smitten because they led Israel into sin through seduction and idolatry, showing the spiritual nature of Israel’s enemies.
